key_insight: INCARBench shows that LLMs can often produce semantically plausible VASP INCAR settings, but scientifically valid configuration still fails frequently when parameters are tightly coupled.
engineering_relevance: For computational materials workflows, reliable AI assistance must satisfy interdependent physics constraints—not just generate seemingly correct input files.
method: Built INCARBench to evaluate LLMs on VASP INCAR configuration generation.
Added a repair task to test whether models can fix incorrect settings while preserving valid ones.
Compared 19 model configurations across semantic, policy, and task-critical correctness.
evidence_signal: Across 19 model configurations, several models scored well on semantic and policy accuracy, but task-critical correctness remained much lower, especially for DFT+U, magnetism, and correlated-material settings.
watch_item: High preservation error in repair tasks suggests that even when LLMs can detect issues, they may still alter already-valid configuration details in scientifically harmful ways.
paper_title: INCARBench: A Benchmark for Scientific Configuration in VASP INCAR by Large Language Models
